If he thinks that this is real justice, does this still count for Ash? >> Okay, look, it's a very sensitive topic—Hitler and the Holocaust. I don't want to spend too much time on it, okay? But if you truly understand Zoroa, what it would say is that Ara Masta means complete forgiveness, compassion, and love. So whatever we do in this world will be forgiven in the end. I know this is hard for many people to accept. We grew up knowing there must be evil in the world because of the Holocaust, and there must be Satan, but if you really want to discover Asha, you have to let go of these ideas and understand that everything will be forgiven in the end.

But if you hate someone in this world and think they deserve hell for what they've done, you need to let go of this hatred. We need to let go of judgment. The very point of Asha is to focus on yourself—don't compare yourself to others. Compare yourself to yourself. The problem keeping us from Asha are our ego and fear. We want to be liked by everyone, but we also fear rejection or offending someone politically. Like I know that in my class, I offend a lot of people and get shot at all the time on YouTube. But if I want to achieve Asha, I need to take this risk because what matters is my own individual pursuit of truth.

What others think of me doesn't matter. Our society brainwashes us into thinking that opinions from teachers or the world matter because they decide our future and status. Zoroastrians, Nichis, Platos, all say that it doesn't matter; true happiness and enlightenment come from a personal journey of solitude and rejecting past knowledge to rebuild ourselves.

Once you make this decision, action will come naturally. But first, let go of prejudices and ideas imposed on you. I know I'll get shouted out and cursed online for saying Hitler will be forgiven because everyone will be forgiven. There is no hell; it's what we create in our hearts. Everyone will be forgiven.

Any more questions? >> My question would be that Asha for everyone will have different meanings but like will it change as I grow up? Um, I'm not a Zorashian priest and don't want to insult the religion, okay? They'll tell you that at the end of the day, Asha is virtue and God is virtue. So when you do Asha, you're moving towards perfection. But Nichis would say, maybe thus but definitely creativity.
